dublinCore.title: Even and Odd Signal Decomposition
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal processing
Signals and systems
Even signals
Odd signals
Signal symmetry
dublinCore.description: Decompose a preset or hand-drawn signal x(t) into its even part x_e(t) = [x(t) + x(-t)]/2 and odd part x_o(t) = [x(t) - x(-t)]/2, read the worked calculation at a probe time, and verify that the two parts sum back to x(t).
relation: Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems

searchKeywords: even and odd parts of a signal

learningObjectives: Explain even and odd symmetry in terms of reflection about t = 0
Apply the decomposition formulas to compute the even and odd parts of a signal at a given time
Verify that the even and odd parts sum to the original signal
Recognize the even and odd parts of pulses, triangles, sawtooth waves and one-sided exponentials
prerequisites: Time reversal and time shifting of signals

misconceptions.misconception: Every signal is either even or odd
misconceptions.correction: Most signals are neither; every signal is the sum of an even part and an odd part
misconceptions.evidence: Select the pulse with a 1 s time shift: both parts are nonzero and the panel reports 50% even and 50% odd

misconceptions.misconception: The even part of a signal is the portion of the signal for t > 0
misconceptions.correction: Both parts are defined for all t and each combines x(t) with x(-t)
misconceptions.evidence: With the pulse at a 1 s shift, x(-1) = 0 but x_e(-1) = 0.5 and x_o(-1) = -0.5

misconceptions.misconception: Shifting a signal in time does not change its even and odd parts
misconceptions.correction: Shifting moves the signal away from its mirror image and changes both parts and the energy split
misconceptions.evidence: The pulse at shift 0 s is 100% even; at shift 1 s it is 50% even and 50% odd

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Three stacked plots from minus five to plus five seconds showing a signal, its even part and its odd part, with a probe time whose values are worked through the decomposition formulas. The signal is chosen from presets or drawn with the mouse.

controls.label: Signal
controls.description: Chooses a preset waveform or a custom signal drawn with the mouse

controls.label: Show sum
controls.description: Shows or hides the purple dashed curve x_e(t) + x_o(t) that lies on top of x(t)

controls.label: Clear
controls.description: Replaces the signal with zero and switches to the custom signal so a new one can be drawn

controls.label: Time shift t0
controls.description: Slides the preset waveform along the time axis; disabled for a custom signal

controls.label: Probe time t
controls.description: Picks the instant t used in the worked calculation; the mirror point -t is marked with an open dot

visualElements.description: Three stacked plots on a shared time axis: x(t) in blue with the dashed purple sum, the even part in green, the odd part in red; dragging inside the top plot draws a custom x(t)
Calculation panel with x(t), x(-t), the even and odd parts, the check sum and the energy split

model.description: Samples x(t) every 0.01 s on a grid symmetric about t = 0 and forms x_e and x_o from x(t) and x(-t); energies are sums of squares over the displayed -5 s to +5 s window

instructionalStrategies: Predict the even and odd parts by hand, then check against the calculation panel
Move the probe to t and -t to see the same two samples combine with opposite signs
extensions: Add a second preset family such as sinusoids with a phase offset
Show the cosine and sine series terms that correspond to the even and odd parts of a periodic signal
